_comments._: JSON has no comments, so the worked example lives here. Delete this whole _comments key before you submit -- the validator ignores it either way, but a merged row should not carry instructions in its manifest.
_comments.schema: Always the literal string 'sabot-submission/1'. Do not change it.
_comments.slug: Directory name under submissions/. One row = one directory. Convention: <framework>-<config>-<model>, lowercase, hyphens.
_comments.submitted: ISO date you opened the pull request.
_comments.sabot_commit: Full 40-character SHA of the sabot commit you ran against. The tasks, operators, anchor table and scorers all come from that commit.
_comments.provenance: Always the literal string 'third-party'. Submitted rows publish in their own table and are never pooled into the author-run medians or the headline. This field is how that separation is enforced mechanically.
_comments.spec_version: The tagged SPEC revision you scored against. Must match the SPEC.md in the commit you ran. A row may not cite an untagged revision.
_comments.protocol: 'wave1-mapping' if you scored only the SPEC section 5 mapping surface. 'wave2-union' if you also ran the anomaly-first FLAGS protocol (SPEC section 10) and are claiming the union surface.
_comments.framework: id is the lowercase slug that appears in every trace's `framework` field. version is an exact pin -- no ranges, no ^ or >=.
_comments.dependency_pins: Everything else whose version could move a number: the agent SDK, the model client, the orchestration layer. Exact pins only.
_comments.config: Which of the two rows this is. name is free text ('default', 'guardrail', ...) and must match every trace's `config` field. description says what the review or guardrail machinery actually is, in enough detail that a reader can rebuild it.
_comments.pipeline_model: The one model serving every agent in the pipeline, uniform across every run (SPEC section 6, fairness by uniformity).
_comments.replicate_labels: At least five. These are LABELS, not random seeds -- if you did not pass them to an RNG, do not call them seeds. Directory names under traces/<task>/<operator>/ are these labels verbatim.
_comments.spend_usd: What the row cost you to produce. Published with the row.
_comments.traces: {"in_repo": true} when the corpus ships in this directory. For a large corpus, {"tarball_url": "https://...", "sha256": "<64 hex>"} instead -- but CI validates only what is in-repo, so an external corpus is verified by the maintainer locally before the row lands.
_comments.carve_outs: Structural carve-outs, in the SPEC 10.6 pattern: an operator whose fault cannot land in view of any component of your pipeline. These cells are never run and leave the matrix entirely -- they are not exclusions and not zeros. Each one needs a reason and a spec_ref, and the merged row is published with the carve-out named. Delete the key if you have none.
_comments.exclusions: Every cell that did not produce a scored result, itemized one by one, never silently dropped. code is one of BASELINE_FAIL, RUN_ERROR, INJECTION_UNVERIFIED (SPEC section 3). A RUN_ERROR or INJECTION_UNVERIFIED exclusion must still ship its runresult.json -- the quarantined trace is what makes the exclusion auditable. Delete the key if you have none.
_comments.claimed: The row you are claiming. Every counter is {hits, n} and every one is recomputed from your raw traces by this repo's committed scorers; a mismatch of one cell fails validation. clean_baseline_false_anchor is the false-anchor base rate on your clean baselines -- run the validator, read the BASE_RATE line, and publish what it prints.

config.name: default
config.description: Hand-rolled multi-agent shape (load -> worker -> review -> revise|emit); review is an LLM reviewer using the verdict-token protocol (SPEC section 5); one revise loop; no deterministic guardrail.
